scenes.tts: A gene is needed for hearing, and its protein sits in the right place. Is that enough to call it the channel? Start with the current.
scenes.visual: Title card: One Current, Three Factors. A gene icon and a protein icon at the lower end of a tip link. Question on screen: enough to call it the channel?
scenes.narration: A gene is needed for hearing, and its protein sits in the right place. Is that enough to call it the channel? Start with the current.

scenes.tts: A hair bundle is a staircase of stereocilia, in rows that rise in height.
scenes.visual: A hair bundle: three rows of stereocilia rising from left to right like a staircase.
scenes.narration: A hair bundle is a staircase of stereocilia, in rows that rise in height.

scenes.tts: Tip links connect the tip of each shorter stereocilium to the side of its taller neighbour.
scenes.visual: Thin lines appear from each shorter tip to the side of the taller neighbour. Label: tip link.
scenes.narration: Tip links connect the tip of each shorter stereocilium to the side of its taller neighbour.

scenes.tts: Deflect the bundle toward its tallest row. The tip links are thought to pull channels open near their lower ends.
scenes.visual: An arrow pushes the bundle toward the tallest row; the tip links stretch, and a small gold channel at the lower end of one link opens. Label: thought to sit here.
scenes.narration: Deflect the bundle toward its tallest row. The tip links are thought to pull channels open near their lower ends.

scenes.tts: With the cell held at a negative voltage, cations flow in, and the current is inward. This is the conventional transduction current.
scenes.visual: Plus signs stream into the stereocilium. A current trace beneath steps downward (inward). Beside it: holding voltage negative, below E_rev. Label: conventional transduction current = opened by deflection toward the tallest row.
scenes.narration: With the cell held at a negative voltage, cations flow in, and the current is inward. This is the conventional transduction current.

scenes.tts: The current rises within a fraction of a millisecond. That is too fast for a chain of second messengers. So force is thought to open the channel directly.
scenes.visual: The trace's rising edge is magnified; a timer reads: within a fraction of a millisecond. A second-messenger cascade beside it is labelled too slow. Arrow from the tip link to the channel: short latency supports direct gating (thought).
scenes.narration: The current rises within a fraction of a millisecond. That is too fast for a chain of second messengers. So force is thought to open the channel directly.

scenes.tts: Plot the size of the peak current against bundle displacement. The S-shaped curve saturates when nearly all channels are open.
scenes.visual: Axes: bundle displacement (x), size of the peak inward current (y). An upward S-shaped curve draws itself and flattens at the top. Label: nearly all channels open = saturation.
scenes.narration: Plot the size of the peak current against bundle displacement. The S-shaped curve saturates when nearly all channels are open.

scenes.tts: That current comes from many channels. Three things set it.
scenes.visual: The single trace splits into three stacked counters, empty for now, multiplying toward I.
scenes.narration: That current comes from many channels. Three things set it.

scenes.tts: First, how many working channels sit at the tip links. Call that N.
scenes.visual: Counter 1 lights: N = number of working channels at the tip links.
scenes.narration: First, how many working channels sit at the tip links. Call that N.

scenes.tts: Second, how much current one open channel passes. That is the unitary current, small i.
scenes.visual: Counter 2 lights: i = unitary current, the current through one open channel. A single step-like event is shown.
scenes.narration: Second, how much current one open channel passes. That is the unitary current, small i.

scenes.tts: Third, the chance that each channel is open. That is the open probability, P open.
scenes.visual: Counter 3 lights: P_open = open probability, the chance a channel is open.
scenes.narration: Third, the chance that each channel is open. That is the open probability, P_open.
scenes.caption: Third, the chance that each channel is open. That is the open probability, P_open.

scenes.tts: For channels that are alike, multiply the three. That gives the average current from the whole bundle.
scenes.visual: On screen: mean I = N × i × P_open (channels alike, fixed voltage and ions). Made-up ensemble: 100 × (−15 pA) × 0.20 = −300 pA. Small note: N and P_open are teaching assumptions.
scenes.narration: For channels that are alike, multiply the three. That gives the average current from the whole bundle.

scenes.tts: Predict. A mutation halves that average current. Which of the three factors did it change?
scenes.visual: Mean level at half size. Text: −300 pA becomes −150 pA. Which factor changed? N? i? P_open?
scenes.narration: Predict. A mutation halves that average current. Which of the three factors did it change?

scenes.tts: From the average alone, you cannot tell. Halve the channels, the unitary current, or the open probability. Each gives the same average current.
scenes.visual: Three panels: N halved, i halved, P_open halved. Each noisy trace settles around the same −150 pA mean line, but their flicker differs. Label: same mean current.
scenes.narration: From the average alone, you cannot tell. Halve the channels, the unitary current, or the open probability. Each gives the same average current.

scenes.tts: A trafficking factor, an anchor or a lipid-modifying enzyme could all be needed. Deleting any one would silence the cell.
scenes.visual: Three suspect cards: trafficking factor, anchor, lipid-modifying enzyme. Each points to a flat trace.
scenes.narration: A trafficking factor, an anchor or a lipid-modifying enzyme could all be needed. Deleting any one would silence the cell.

scenes.tts: So a lost current cannot tell you which factor you removed.
scenes.visual: Rule card, line 1: a lost current cannot say which factor you removed.
scenes.narration: So a lost current cannot tell you which factor you removed.

scenes.tts: Evidence about permeation speaks more directly to the pore. Which ions pass, and how much current does one open channel carry?
scenes.visual: Rule card, line 2: permeation speaks more directly to the pore. Ion icons pass through one open channel; the i counter and a selectivity label glow.
scenes.narration: Evidence about permeation speaks more directly to the pore. Which ions pass, and how much current does one open channel carry?

scenes.tts: So do a residue reached in a working channel, and activity of the protein on its own. But partners can change permeation too. So the case rests on several rungs together.
scenes.visual: Rule card, line 3: plus a reachable residue and activity of the protein alone; partners can change permeation too, so the case rests on several rungs. Two partner shapes appear beside the channel.
scenes.narration: So do a residue reached in a working channel, and activity of the protein on its own. But partners can change permeation too. So the case rests on several rungs together.

scenes.tts: Carry one question through every experiment. Which factor did it test, and what did it rule out?
scenes.visual: Takeaway card: I = N × i × P_open, with the question: which factor did it test, and what did it rule out?
scenes.narration: Carry one question through every experiment. Which factor did it test, and what did it rule out?
